record.question:
A city is deploying a MySQL-compatible web portal at the zone apex example.com in a Route 53 public hosted zone. The application must continue operating after a single Availability Zone failure, and the database needs a ready failover instance in another AZ. Application instances are stateless. The team must avoid maintaining DNS records containing individual load-balancer IP addresses.

Which design meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an ALB and an Auto Scaling group across two AZs with an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Create a non-alias A record at example.com containing the ALB’s current IP addresses.
Use an ALB and an Auto Scaling group across three AZs. Use Aurora MySQL with a writer and replicas in other AZs, and create an A alias record at example.com targeting the ALB.
Use an ALB and an Auto Scaling group across three AZs with an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance and read replicas. Create a CNAME record at example.com targeting the ALB DNS name.
Use an ALB and an Auto Scaling group across three AZs. Use one Aurora MySQL writer without any replica instances, and create an A alias record at example.com targeting the ALB.

explanation.text:
<<2>> combines compute capacity across AZs, database failover compute in another AZ and a Route 53 alias that tracks the ALB endpoint. Aurora’s distributed storage and separately placed replica instances provide different parts of database resilience.

<<1>> has a suitable availability foundation but pins DNS to changing ALB addresses. <<3>> uses a CNAME at the hosted-zone apex, where CNAME records are not permitted. A CNAME can be valid for a subdomain, so it is the apex requirement that eliminates this choice. <<4>> has durable multi-AZ Aurora storage but lacks the requested ready replica instance for failover.

An alias can be an A record: “alias” describes Route 53 target resolution, while A is the DNS record type. Size surviving application capacity for the AZ failure and test connection recovery; a multi-AZ diagram does not itself guarantee a numerical RTO.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-elb-load-balancer.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.Reliability.html

diagram_alt: An apex alias prevents fixed ALB address maintenance while separate compute and database replicas provide AZ resilience.

sources.supports: A alias records support ELB targets at zone apexes; CNAME records support subdomains only.
Aurora replicas across AZs improve availability beyond its replicated storage.

editorial_notes: Added an explicit zone-apex constraint, replacing the false claim that CNAME is always unsuitable for ALB.
Replaced unspecified strict RPO/RTO language with concrete single-AZ failure requirements.
